changeReason: Reduce CP2077 start latency and add startup/warmup diagnostics on top of the published depth-probe-v2026.09.18 baseline (D3D11 4 / D3D12 8, DLL sha256:cea4784dcb45dee18aaeb58dd0b8d3b32727c0b9f32fb30b9e93bfcb454f9e55). Object location during StartRun now settles memory readability once per queried VirtualQuery region instead of issuing one query per fixed-size read; the per-address verdict, the audited exact-build chain and every failure path are unchanged, and reads still go through fallible ReadProcessMemory so a region revoked mid-walk fails closed rather than access-violating. On hardware the probe went from 10.34 s to 1.05 s between the start command and Started, where 5,827 queries previously cost 9.62 s of it. A control-thread-only startup_timing harness records phase wall clocks, VirtualQuery counts and scan counts into one log line per run; its scope is thread-local, so periodic audits and render-thread reads stay outside the report. Warmup now attributes blocked Presents through a fixed-width blocker bitmap and emits one warmup_timing summary when warmup completes. The readiness rule (8 consecutive qualified Presents, at least 500 ms of span, no gap above 125 ms) and every blocker verdict, including the if/else-if chain that reports only the first camera failure, decide exactly as before; the per-Present path allocates nothing and takes no lock, and the summary is skipped when its lock is contended. These diagnostics never feed admission, capture, matrix, coverage or loss gates, and no log is written per memory read. Impact is declared none: both generations are retained, so the existing D3D11 generation-4 and D3D12 generation-8 performance certifications stay applicable to the new DLL. The system anticipates this case; ApprovedProbeRuntime is documented as allowing multiple SHA values to carry the same pair of reviewed generations. The two backends are retained on different strengths of evidence, and both are stated here so a reviewer can contest either one directly. D3D11: the CP2077 object-location change gives D3D11 nothing, and its only share is the warmup instrumentation, because hooked_present dispatches D3D12 swapchains to hooked_present_d3d12 and returns, leaving its tail as the D3D11 path. That share is a bounded net addition: per non-qualified Present it computes a blocker bitmap and increments a fixed 13-entry array, with no allocation, lock or syscall, on the order of tens of nanoseconds against a 33 ms frame budget, and it is skipped entirely once formal capture is armed because the warmup branch is the else arm of formal_at_present. The one exception is the watermark_only measurement stage, where formal_at_present && !watermark_only() is false and the branch is still reached after arming. D3D12: the retained generation rests on a code-level direction argument, not on a measurement, and that limit is recorded deliberately. audit_formal_player runs on the control thread roughly every 100 ms for the whole recording, so the changed code does execute inside the window a performance certification measures; there it now issues far fewer VirtualQuery calls and therefore holds the address-space lock for less time, which can only reduce contention with the game's own memory activity. No steady-state frame-time A/B was run: the measured evidence in this change covers StartRun latency only. The existing CP2077 certification is also narrow (1% low -1.22% against +/-10% same-stage noise, and +31% on Full frames above 36 ms), so carrying it forward is a judgement about direction rather than margin. The repository owner ruled on 2026-09-21 to carry the existing D3D12 certification forward on that basis and to skip the paired frame-time run; if a reviewer disagrees, the remedy is one paired short recording comparing perf-frames.jsonl before and after, not a re-derivation from this text. Independent of these generations, the new exact DLL bytes still require artifact publication and central runtime approval, because approval matches on the DLL SHA-256 as well as the generation pair; existing exact-runtime approvals are neither removed nor transferred. The duplicate CaptureWarmupObservation::blockers implementation was removed and its text is now derived from the single blocker_flags predicate, which both backends use. Runtime version depth-2026.09.19 is unpublished and distinct from the published depth-2026.09.18. Windows cargo test -p dm-depth-probe reports 537 passed / 0 failed, including the pre-existing lifecycle_warmup_timeout_diagnostics_name_the_actual_blockers case that pins the blocker text. This declaration now also covers the client version bump from 0.7.33 to 0.7.34, which touches Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock. The generation gate counts both as probe inputs, so the declaration must move with them even though no probe source, verdict or behaviour changed: the bump only renumbers the workspace and its members. Generations stay 4/8 and the impact stays none for the same reasons recorded above; nothing in this bump touches either backend's capture, admission or per-Present work. runtimeVersion deliberately stays depth-2026.09.19, because dataminer-release.yml derives the expected R2 prefix from it and the client bundles the already published depth-2026.09.19 artifact (sha256:ba332751eed91a60359b03dfcf007ebd95ad0dee6da42aad010b8c9119df2deb); renaming the runtime here would point the release at an artifact that does not exist. One hazard is recorded for whoever publishes the next probe: dm-depth-probe takes version.workspace, so a probe rebuilt from this tree carries different bytes than the published depth-2026.09.19 artifact, while DM_DEPTH_PROBE_RUNTIME_VERSION would still make it declare the same runtime identity. The next probe release must therefore take a new runtimeVersion rather than reuse this one; the published artifact above remains the only depth-2026.09.19 bytes in approvedRuntimes.
